chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn narrated, saying:
Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام said to me: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has allies with the ruler through whom He repels from His allies.”

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: The kunyah of Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام in this narration
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَ: Allies or devoted servants under Allah’s care
key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: His awliya', meaning those beloved and loyal to Allah
key_terms.يَدْفَعُ: He repels or wards off harm

ai.seo_question: How does Allah protect His awliya' through people close to rulers?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, may place certain loyal servants within the sphere of political authority to protect His awliya'. It highlights divine wisdom in governance and shows that not everyone associated with rulers is necessarily outside the service of truth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3664 - It is narrated from Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:
Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) said to me: 'Indeed, Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, has allies among the rulers through whom He (swt) repels harm from His (swt) friends.'
